title: Empty evidence queries produce title matches for every course
reasoning: When `context.rawQuery` is empty or whitespace, `normalizedRaw` becomes an empty string. Since every non-empty title includes the empty string, the title-match condition adds `Title match: ...` evidence for every course even though the user provided no title text. This can mislead filter-only or advanced-search responses by manufacturing keyword evidence.
reproduction: Call `buildMatchEvidence` with a course titled `Data Structures`, `rawQuery: ''`, and an otherwise empty plan. The returned evidence includes a `title` item even though there is no raw query text to match.
recommendation: Require a non-empty normalized raw query before checking title containment. Consider token-aware matching or a minimum normalized query length to avoid similarly broad one-character title matches.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The course DTO evidence tests exercise non-empty raw queries such as `CS 225`, `easy ...`, and `counts for something`; they do not cover empty or whitespace-only raw queries.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a `buildMatchEvidence` test with `rawQuery: ''` and another with whitespace, asserting that no `title` evidence is produced.
